description: The chooser, in the detail card only. Automatic resolution stays byte for byte as cheap and as quiet as FEAT-002 leaves it: first hit wins, silently, and nothing in the library hints that alternatives exist. Opening a game's detail sheet, and only that, enumerates every candidate for it (each folder of its own system, plus cross-system matches), shows each as a selectable thumbnail labelled with what it is and where it came from, marks the one in use, and keeps the existing Choose an image from Files action beside a new return-to-automatic action. A chosen cover is persisted against the entry's stable id, outranks every automatic resolve, and survives relaunch. Depends on FEAT-002 for the per-folder lists, the alignment and the cross-system order.
steps: NEW FILE native/ios/ArtworkChooser.swift, and add it to native/ios/project.yml under targets.Continuum.sources with a comment saying what it is. An unlisted file is silently never compiled, so this is the first step, not the last. Keep every pure declaration in it a COLUMN-0 enum or struct so .work/artwork-probe/make-harness.py can extract it.

ArtworkChooser.swift, the pure option. `struct ArtworkOption: Identifiable, Sendable, Equatable` with: `system: GameSystem` (whose thumbnail directory the URL addresses), `folder: ThumbnailFolder`, `thumbnailName: String` (the listing filename with .png dropped), `url: URL`, `isCrossSystem: Bool`, and `var id: String` built as "\(system.rawValue)#\(folder.rawValue)#\(thumbnailName)" so it is STABLE across launches, which is what lets a persisted choice be recognised again. `var label: String` returns `folder.readableName` for an own-system option and "\(folder.readableName) from \(system.displayName)" for a cross-system one, for example "box art", "title screen", "in-game shot", "box art from Game Boy". Derive it from the existing vocabulary, never a second copy of those words.

ArtworkChooser.swift, the pure enumeration. `enum ArtworkOptions` with `static func enumerate(query: String, ownSystem: GameSystem, lists: [(system: GameSystem, folder: ThumbnailFolder, titles: [String: String])]) -> [ArtworkOption]`. For each list in the order given, take the exact match and every aligned title (`ArtworkIndexNames.match` plus `ArtworkIndexNames.alignedTitles`, so the chooser deliberately shows the AMBIGUOUS matches automatic resolution refused: ambiguity becomes a user choice instead of a coin flip), build one option per distinct listing filename, and dedupe by URL. Own-system lists come first in `ThumbnailFolder.allCases` order, then cross-system lists in `SystemArtwork.crossSystemListOrder` order. Pure and Foundation-only, so the harness runs it against the real saved listings.

ArtworkChooser.swift, the persisted choice. `struct ArtworkChoice: Codable, Sendable, Equatable` with `kind` (an enum with `remote` and `pickedFile`), `systemRaw: String?`, `folderRaw: String?`, `thumbnailName: String?`, `address: String?`, `label: String`, `chosenAt: Double`. Plus `enum ArtworkChoices` holding the pure map codec: `static func decode(_ data: Data?) -> [String: ArtworkChoice]` and `static func encode(_ map: [String: ArtworkChoice]) -> Data?`, so the whole map is one JSON blob in UserDefaults under the NEW key "continuum.artwork.choice.v1". Keyed on `ArtworkDisk.key(forPath:)`, exactly as continuum.artwork.misses.v1 and continuum.artwork.sources.v1 are, so all per-entry artwork state shares one key space.

ArtworkStore.swift, the address map. Add "continuum.artwork.address.v1", a `[String: String]` of disk key to the ADDRESS the stored cover came from, written wherever `recordProvenance` is written and cleared wherever it is cleared. It exists so the chooser can mark the option currently in use by URL rather than by guessing from a readable sentence. When the in-use address matches no enumerated option, the chooser shows the stored cover itself as a first, non-selectable in-use row labelled with its provenance string.

ArtworkStore.swift, the chooser's data, none of it published. Add, all @MainActor on the existing store: `func artworkChoice(for entry: LibraryEntry) -> ArtworkChoice?`; `func cachedArtworkOptions(for entry: LibraryEntry) -> [ArtworkOption]?` reading a plain (non-@Published) `[String: [ArtworkOption]]` cache keyed on the disk key, so reopening the sheet is free; `func enumerateArtworkOptions(for entry: LibraryEntry, system: GameSystem, includeCrossSystemDownloads: Bool) async -> [ArtworkOption]`; `func artworkOptionThumbnail(_ option: ArtworkOption) async -> UIImage?`; `func chooseArtwork(_ option: ArtworkOption, for entry: LibraryEntry) async`; `func clearArtworkChoice(for entry: LibraryEntry)`. Do NOT add @Published properties for the option list or the thumbnails: the library shell observes this store, so publishing per-thumbnail state would rebuild the whole shell for every image that arrives. The sheet owns that state (next step).

ArtworkStore.swift, enumeration cost discipline. `enumerateArtworkOptions` runs ONLY from the sheet, never from `resolve`, `runSweep` or `cover(for:)`. It gathers the game's own system's three lists (downloading a missing one, announced through the existing announce-before-download path, because the user just asked) plus every OTHER (system, folder) list already in memory or on disk with NO download. With `includeCrossSystemDownloads: true`, which only the explicit button below sets, it additionally downloads the remaining Named_Boxarts lists in `SystemArtwork.crossSystemListOrder` order, cheapest first, one at a time, checking `Task.isCancelled` between them so closing the sheet stops it. It caches its result under the disk key and reuses the same one-task-per-(system, folder) discipline for every list it needs.

ArtworkStore.swift, thumbnails. `artworkOptionThumbnail` checks a store-owned `NSCache<NSString, UIImage>` keyed on the option's URL (countLimit and totalCostLimit set the same way the cover cache is, with the same per-image cost function), then on a miss acquires `ArtworkGate`, GETs the URL on `ArtworkFetcher.session`, validates status 200 and an image/ Content-Type exactly as `ArtworkFetcher.resolve` does, decodes off the main actor, releases the gate, caches and returns. Nothing between acquire and release may throw. A failure returns nil and writes a distinct artwork line naming the option's label.

ArtworkStore.swift, choosing. `chooseArtwork` downloads the option through `ArtworkGate` (or reuses the thumbnail cache's bytes if it has them), stores them at the entry's disk key through `ArtworkDisk.store`, records the choice in continuum.artwork.choice.v1, records the provenance as "chosen: \(option.label)" and the address, clears any remembered miss, bumps `generation` so every card refreshes, and reports a distinct line. `clearArtworkChoice` removes the choice record, removes the stored cover and the address, clears the miss so automatic resolution can run again, bumps `generation` and reports.

ArtworkStore.swift, a choice outranks everything. In `resolve(entry:system:key:)`, after the existing step 1 (a cover already on disk wins, which is the path a chosen cover normally takes) and BEFORE step 2, add: if a choice exists for this key and there is no cover on disk, restore THE CHOICE rather than walking the ladder. For `.remote`, re-download the chosen address through `ArtworkGate` and keep it with the chosen label. For `.pickedFile` the bytes were the only copy, so drop the record and write a distinct line saying the picked image is gone and automatic artwork will be used. An automatic resolve must never overwrite a live choice, and this is the one place that could have.

ArtworkStore.swift, the existing actions keep their promises. `clearCover(for:)` (Remove the stored cover) also clears that entry's choice and address, and says so. `lookUpAgain(_:)` also clears the choice and says so, because tapping it means go and find it automatically. `clearStoredCovers()` keeps `.remote` choices, which can be downloaded again, and DROPS `.pickedFile` choices, whose bytes were the only copy, and reports how many of each went. `forgetCoverLists()` is untouched: it clears every per-folder list, which is what `ArtworkCoverLists.clear()` already does by emptying the directory.

ArtworkStore.swift, clean up deleted games. `sweepLibrary(_ entries:)` is handed the whole library after every rescan (ContinuumApp.refreshLibrary calls it), so prune there: build the set of `ArtworkDisk.key(forPath:)` for the entries and drop any key absent from it out of continuum.artwork.choice.v1, continuum.artwork.address.v1, continuum.artwork.sources.v1 and continuum.artwork.misses.v1, plus the option cache. Guard it with `guard !entries.isEmpty` and say why in the comment: a rescan that found nothing because the directory could not be read must not wipe the state of a library that is still there. This is the one place per-entry artwork state is pruned, and all four maps share the key space, so they are pruned together.

NEW in ArtworkChooser.swift, the sheet's model. `@MainActor final class ArtworkChooserModel: ObservableObject` with `@Published private(set) var options: [ArtworkOption]`, `@Published private(set) var thumbnails: [String: UIImage]` keyed on option id, `@Published private(set) var inUseOptionID: String?`, `@Published private(set) var isWorking: Bool`, `@Published private(set) var line: String`, and `func load(entry:system:store:)` that returns immediately if it has already loaded (so a body re-evaluation cannot re-enumerate), reads the cached options first, then enumerates, then resolves thumbnails PROGRESSIVELY (one child task per option, each publishing as it lands, so the sheet never blocks and the ArtworkGate caps concurrency), plus `func searchOtherSystems(...)`, `func choose(...)` and `func useAutomatic(...)`. Cancel outstanding work in `deinit` is not available on a @MainActor class holding tasks, so keep a `[Task<Void, Never>]` and cancel it from `.onDisappear` in the sheet.

GameDetailSheet.swift, the section. Keep the existing COVER ART heading and the Source read-out. Add a `@StateObject private var chooser = ArtworkChooserModel()` and a `.task` that calls `chooser.load` once, so enumeration happens on open and never during browsing. Lay the options out as a horizontal row of thumbnails (a LazyHStack in a horizontal ScrollView, roughly 72 by 96 each, `ArtPlate` under any that has not resolved so nothing is blank), each with its label underneath, each tappable to choose it, and the in-use one marked with a visible border and a checkmark plus an accessibility label saying it is in use. Below the row: the existing "Choose an image from Files" button, a new "Use automatic artwork again" button (enabled only when a choice is recorded), the existing "Look it up again" and "Remove the stored cover" buttons, and a "Look in other systems for more covers" button whose SettingsNote says plainly that it downloads other systems' cover lists smallest first and that all nine box art lists together are about 11 MB if none of them is already on the device. With exactly one option the row shows that one thumbnail marked in use and reads as a statement, not an error: no counts, no empty state, no "1 of 1".

GameDetailSheet.swift, keep the rest of the sheet as it is: the header cover, the facts, the Play and Close actions, the cue note and the delete block are unchanged. Nothing in the library, the hero, the shelves, the grid or the list rows changes: no badge, no count, no hint that alternatives exist. That is the requirement, not an omission.

Harness: extend .work/artwork-probe/make-harness.py to extract ArtworkOption, ArtworkOptions, ArtworkChoice and ArtworkChoices from native/ios/ArtworkChooser.swift (they must be Foundation-only; UIKit and SwiftUI types belong in the model and the view, which the harness does not extract). Add checks, all of which must pass: (1) `ArtworkOptions.enumerate` run against the four real saved listings (gg boxart, gg title, gg snap, gb boxart) for "Simpsons, The - Krusty's Fun House (U) [!].gg" returns exactly four options, in that order, with labels "box art", "title screen", "in-game shot", "box art from Game Boy", each naming Krusty's Fun House (USA, Europe); (2) with only the gg boxart list it returns one option and that is not an error; (3) option ids are stable and unique, and the same (system, folder, name) always produces the same id; (4) a map with two aligning titles produces TWO options for the same folder, proving the chooser offers what auto-selection refused; (5) `ArtworkChoices.encode` then `decode` round-trips a map holding one `.remote` choice and one `.pickedFile` choice with every field intact, and `decode(nil)` is empty rather than a crash; (6) a cross-system option's label always names its system and an own-system option's never does.

Verify, then commit. Run every gate in the verification list, review by eye for @MainActor isolation (no @Published mutated off the main actor, every store method that touches @Published state reached only from the main actor), async cancellation and the no-await-between-check-and-insert rule on every task dictionary. Commit locally on ios-ui-player-controls with a message such as "Let the card choose between every cover the server has for a game". Do NOT push.
acceptance_criteria: Automatic resolution is unchanged in cost and in noise: no enumeration, no extra request and no new status line happens during normal browsing or during the library sweep, and nothing in the library, hero, shelves, grid or list rows indicates that alternatives exist

Opening a game's detail sheet enumerates candidates once, showing every folder of its own system plus cross-system matches, each as a selectable thumbnail labelled "box art", "title screen", "in-game shot" or "box art from Game Boy"
The option currently in use is marked, including the case where the in-use cover came from a ladder name no list carries
With exactly one candidate the section shows that one thumbnail and reads sensibly, with no count and no empty state
Choosing an option stores it at the entry's disk key, records it under continuum.artwork.choice.v1 keyed on ArtworkDisk.key(forPath:), bumps generation so cards refresh, and survives relaunch

A recorded choice outranks automatic resolution: with a choice present and the cover missing from disk, resolve restores the choice instead of walking the ladder, and no automatic path overwrites a live choice
Return-to-automatic clears the choice and lets automatic resolution run again; Choose an image from Files still works exactly as it did and is recorded as a pickedFile choice
Thumbnails resolve progressively, never block the sheet, go through ArtworkGate, and are cached so reopening the sheet costs nothing
Deleting a game drops its choice, address, provenance and miss records on the next library sweep, and an empty rescan prunes nothing
ArtworkChooser.swift appears in native/ios/project.yml under targets.Continuum.sources and project.yml still parses
swiftc -frontend -parse exits 0 for every .swift file under native/ios/, cargo test still reports 74 passed, and the harness passes including all six new checks
verification: cd native/ios && for f in *.swift; do swiftc -frontend -parse "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "ok $f" || echo "FAIL $f"; done

python3 -c "import yaml,glob,os;d=yaml.safe_load(open('native/ios/project.yml'));listed={s['path'] for s in d['targets']['Continuum']['sources']};print('unlisted:',[os.path.basename(p) for p in glob.glob('native/ios/*.swift') if os.path.basename(p) not in listed])"
cd .work/artwork-probe && python3 make-harness.py && swiftc -O -o harness Extracted.swift main.swift && ./harness
grep -n 'enumerateArtworkOptions' native/ios/*.swift (confirm it is called only from ArtworkChooserModel, never from resolve, runSweep or cover(for:))
findings: Committed as 4415ce3. New file native/ios/ArtworkChooser.swift, registered in project.yml. Pure layer: ArtworkOption (id '<system>#<folder>#<name>', label from ThumbnailFolder.readableName plus GameSystem.displayName), ArtworkOptions.enumerate / .enumerated (the async nonisolated wrapper so the up to twelve list scan runs off the main actor) / .summary, ArtworkChoice (+ optionFolder and optionSystem parsed back out of the id) and ArtworkChoices as the JSON codec for UserDefaults key continuum.artwork.choice.v1. Store: optionCache and an NSCache of option thumbnails (both plain, not @Published, so the library shell is not rebuilt), enumerateArtworkOptions (own system's three folders downloaded on open, other systems free from disk, paid pass only on the explicit button), artworkOptionThumbnail (ArtworkGate, ArtworkFetcher validation, ArtworkDisk.decode off the main actor), chooseArtwork, clearArtworkChoice, inUseOptionID via the new continuum.artwork.address.v1 map, restore() called from resolve() step 1b so a choice outranks the ladder, and pruneState() in sweepLibrary guarded on a non-empty library. clearStoredCovers keeps remote choices and drops picked ones; clearCover and lookUpAgain drop the choice and say so; handlePickedArtwork records a pickedFile choice. A ListPhase enum was added so the announce-before-download sentence is true for all three callers (resolving, borrowing, choosing). GameDetailSheet holds the model as a @StateObject, enumerates in .task(id: entry.id), cancels in .onDisappear, and reads the in-use mark and the has-a-choice state from the store so they cannot go stale. Harness 128/128.
